The pre-existing test failures are unrelated to MCP—they're native module issues and OIDC configuration problems. I'm verifying the git safe.directory setup: the global config gets written to /root/.gitconfig when the entrypoint runs as root, which works fine, but when FastAPI refreshes and runs as the `nao` user on the nao-owned repo, we don't actually need the safe.directory setting there.

For the `su nao` command to check write permissions, I'm accounting for edge cases like nologin shells (handled by passing `-s /bin/sh`) and potential PAM messages to stderr, both acceptable. The `set -e` flag plays nicely with the `if !` construct, and using `id -u nao` in the echo is straightforward.

I'm deciding against updating the docs—the entrypoint warning already catches this at runtime, so keeping the change focused is better than adding notes to .env.example or docker-compose READMEs.

The problem isn't an MCP conflict — it's file ownership. In git mode, `docker/entrypoint.sh` clones the repo as root (the entrypoint runs as root since the Dockerfile has no `USER`), but supervisord runs the backend as the `nao` user. Nothing chowns the clone afterwards, so when the MCP service tries to create `agent/mcps/linear/` inside the project folder to write its per-tool OpenAPI specs, it gets `EACCES`. In your case the clone also landed in `/app/example` (the Dockerfile's default `NAO_DEFAULT_PROJECT_PATH`), which was `nao`-owned from the build until the entrypoint did `rm -rf` and re-cloned it as root.

I made two changes:

**`docker/entrypoint.sh`** now chowns the cloned context to `nao:nao` after both the clone and pull paths, so the services can write into it. Because root then operates on a repo owned by another user on subsequent restarts, git would refuse with "dubious ownership", so I register the clone target as a `safe.directory` for root before the clone/pull. I also added a writability pre-flight check that runs for both `git` and `local` modes and prints an actionable warning at startup — local mode has the same failure whenever the bind-mounted folder is root-owned on the host.

**`apps/backend/src/services/mcp.ts`** no longer lets a spec-write failure bubble up. `_writeEnabledSpecs` now wraps the actual file writes and, on failure, records the reason in `_failedConnections[server]` and logs it. That message surfaces as the `error` field in the MCP server status UI, so a read-only context shows one broken MCP server instead of a 500 on every `POST /api/agent`.

For the container that's already running, you don't need to rebuild to unblock it:

```bash
docker exec -u root <container> chown -R nao:nao /app/example
```

One thing worth deciding separately: pointing `NAO_DEFAULT_PROJECT_PATH` at `/app/example` in git mode makes the entrypoint delete the bundled example project and clone over it. It works, but `/app/context` is the path the docs and compose comments assume, and it's pre-created with the right ownership in the Dockerfile. I left the path behavior untouched since I can't tell whether `/app/example` was intentional or just the inherited default.

I need to wrap up by summarizing the solution and noting the immediate workaround for the running container.
